strongest_objection: The loop the form inference leans on does not close, and the item it starts from has its causal order reversed. Pass that stamps the sale says the outside buyer discounts because it knows the insiders 'saw the numbers and passed', but under a right of first refusal the insiders pass only after the outsider has named a price; the real mechanism is anticipated adverse selection: the outsider wins only in the case where the informed holders chose not to match, so it bids as if it had already lost every case worth winning, and the insiders then match at the price that anticipation produced. The edge First to know it is dying → Pass that stamps the sale then claims the spoiled price 'returns as a lower mark on the insiders' own position', which is unsupported twice over: NVCA-form refusal rights burden key holders' transfers, not the investors' preferred, so the insiders' shares never pass through the gate they hold, and funds mark to the last round's price rather than to a founder's discounted secondary. The lag and the refusal are a dependency (the lag is what makes the refusal informative), not a loop. Second and nearly as heavy: Successor in the chair lists 'a fund in wind-down that needs distributions' among its successors, which is the same holder with a later clock and is exactly the biting case Threshold that ends independence already carries, so the two items share one illustration and the sharp cut between them (a different decision-maker versus the same decision-maker aged) is not made; and its edge asserts that 'no wording of the veto prevents' the passage while the map's own wild priority proposes the clause that would. Everything else survived real pressure: the payoff-slope pair is exact, the ratchet-as-waiver reading is the map's genuine discovery, and the two closing items pass the type only because the of-sentence's holder clause admits them, which the map says out loud.

items.item: Dividend in the drawer: a cumulative dividend that is never paid accrues into the preference, so the claim on an exit grows with the calendar and with nothing else, as an eight percent cumulative on a growth round turns a one-times preference into roughly one and two-thirds after seven years while the common's share of the same sale shrinks each year the company does not sell; not the preference itself but its slope in time, worthless in the fast rich exit where the preferred converts and fatal in the slow modest one, where the years bought by patience were paid out of the common.
items.why: It fails the map's own type and its own boundary. The of-sentence asks for a term that carries power beyond its price in a future state with a holder who exercises it; an accruing cumulative dividend is a claim that self-executes in the waterfall, nobody exercises anything, and boundary claim four sends 'every route by which ownership drains other than through a power in a state' to another map. It is also the one item that duplicates a sibling in this fleet nearly verbatim (dilution-carriers' Dividend nobody pays, same eight-percent case, same 'grows on a clock' mechanism). The exact figure is also under-specified: eight percent for seven years is 1.56x simple and 1.71x compounded, and NVCA-form cumulative dividends are simple unless drafted otherwise, so 'roughly one and two-thirds' assumes compounding the item never states. The seriation's front stop survives the cut: Redemption clock already opens with 'a redemption date arrives'. If a dividend belongs on this map at all it is as a waiver chip, the accrued dividend payable in cash on conversion at a listing that the underwriters require the holder to forgive, which is a power in a state and would sit beside Ratchet that must be waived; that is a new item for another breath, not a repair of this one.

items.item: Pass that stamps the sale: a right of first refusal on transfers, held by the parties who also hold the information, makes every secondary sale a signal, since the outside buyer knows the insiders saw the numbers and passed, so the founder or angel who needs liquidity finds the outsider's price discounted by the insiders' refusal and the insiders able to buy at that discount; not a price set for the stranger's eyes but a refusal read as one, and it bites hardest on the holder who needs the sale most.
items.why: The mechanism is real but the sequence is backwards. Under a right of first refusal the outside buyer names its price first and the insiders match or pass afterwards, so at the moment of bidding there is no refusal to read. The outsider discounts because it will win only in the case where the informed holders chose not to match; that anticipation, not an observed pass, is what spoils the price, and the insiders then match at the spoiled price. The repair keeps the item's strange claim (a refusal that prices) and fixes only the direction of time.
items.repair: Pass that stamps the sale: a right of first refusal on transfers, held by the parties who also hold the information, makes every secondary sale a lemons market before any refusal is given, since the outside buyer wins only in the case where the insiders, who saw the numbers, chose not to match, so it bids as if it had already lost every case worth winning, and the founder or angel who needs liquidity finds the outsider's price discounted by a pass that has not yet happened while the insiders may match at that discount; not a price set for the stranger's eyes but a refusal read before it is given, and it bites hardest on the holder who needs the sale most.

items.item: Successor in the chair: a term is held by an entity and exercised by whoever the entity has become when the state arrives, so the veto priced against a friendly partner is pulled by that partner's replacement, by a fund in wind-down that needs distributions, by a secondary buyer who took the position at a discount and breaks even at a different price, or by a continuation vehicle with a fresh clock, as the drag that was a courtesy at signing and a sale order twelve years later; not the term but the replacement of its holder, and the counterparty of the term was never the counterparty of the negotiation.
items.why: As written it swallows its neighbor. 'A fund in wind-down that needs distributions' is the same holder with a later clock, which is precisely the biting case Threshold that ends independence already carries (the fund past its tenth year pulling the drag), so the two items share one illustration. The distinction that earns this item is a different decision-maker exercising a term a different decision-maker priced: the replacement partner, the secondary buyer with a different basis, the continuation vehicle with a fresh clock, the liquidating general partner handed the book. The repair strikes the aging fund from the successor list and names the cut, so that Threshold that ends independence keeps the clock and this item keeps the person.
items.repair: Successor in the chair: a term is held by an entity and exercised by whoever holds the entity's pen when the state arrives, so the veto priced against a friendly partner is pulled by that partner's replacement, by a secondary buyer who took the position at a discount and breaks even at a different price, by a continuation vehicle with a fresh clock, or by the liquidating manager handed a fund's book in wind-down, as the drag that was a courtesy at signing and a sale order twelve years later from a hand that never signed; not the same holder whose clock has run, which Threshold that ends independence carries, but the replacement of the holder, and the counterparty of the term was never the counterparty of the negotiation.

items.item: Reserves test in loyalty's clothing: pay-to-play converts the preferred of any investor who does not fund its share of the down round into common, or strips its anti-dilution, so it bites on funds without reserves rather than on founders and sorts the syndicate by dry powder under the name of commitment, as the small seed fund in its eighth year whose entire position converts; not a founder's term at all, since the founder is an incidental beneficiary, but a term investors sign against each other while imagining they would always play.
items.why: Pay-to-play is already an admitted item in a grown list the author read: clean-exits' Fade by formula uses 'a venture syndicate's pay-to-play' as its illustration of dilution on a schedule fixed at entry. The brief requires an adjacent item to say what it adds; this one does not name the neighbor. The mechanism here is genuinely different (who the term bites, sorting the syndicate by dry powder under the name of commitment) and worth keeping; the repair adds the discriminator.
items.repair: Reserves test in loyalty's clothing: pay-to-play converts the preferred of any investor who does not fund its share of the down round into common, or strips its anti-dilution, so it bites on funds without reserves rather than on founders and sorts the syndicate by dry powder under the name of commitment, as the small seed fund in its eighth year whose entire position converts; not a founder's term at all, since the founder is an incidental beneficiary, and not the fade by formula that clean-exits carries as the leaver's price fixed at entry, but a term investors sign against each other while imagining they would always play, whose bite is decided by a reserve ledger written at another table.

items.item: Threshold that ends independence: drag-along names the coalition, usually the board plus a preferred majority, that can force every holder to sell, and it bites when the investors' clocks diverge from the company's, as the fund past its tenth year that needs distributions and pulls the drag at a price inside the stack where the common takes nothing; not the minority's same-price protection but the trigger and whose clock sets it, and it is worthless without a buyer, who knows this and prices the drag into the offer.
items.why: Tested as the right-hand neighbor of Successor in the chair; survives once the successor item stops claiming the aging fund. It discriminates itself from clean-exits' Drag and tag explicitly, and the drag-counting dependency in its edge with Stack that sorts the syndicate is real.

items.item: Threshold that quietly disenfranchises: information rights, pro rata, and the rest are granted to a major investor defined by a share count or a dollar figure, so every later round that dilutes a holder below the line strips its powers by arithmetic rather than by any vote, as the seed fund that learns of the sale from the press because it fell out of the definition two rounds earlier; not a term with a bite of its own but the key that decides who holds the others, and its holder is whoever writes the next definition.
items.why: Tested against First to know it is dying as a second neighbor pair; separable (a threshold strips rights with no lag among the remaining holders, and a lag exists among holders who all sit above the line and receive reports on different cadences). The item is sound; its placement on the seriation is not, see the seriation note: a threshold is crossed only when a later issuance dilutes the holder, which is an outside arrival, not the calendar.

items.item: New money rewrites the old paper: any term that bites only through an outside arrival can be made a condition of the arrival, so the new lead demands the ratchet waived, the stack collapsed, pay-to-play imposed, or every earlier preferred converted to common at a fraction, and the old terms are worth at most what the arrival is worth to their holders, as in the recapitalization that turns three rounds of preferences into common in one afternoon; not a term but the state that reprices terms, and the true counterparty of a state-contingent power is whoever supplies the state.
items.why: Tested against the type. It is not a term and says so; it passes because the of-sentence's clause about terms 'whose only cash value is the price of their own waiver' makes the arrival's demand for waiver the exercise of those terms, with the new lead as holder. The carrier that makes this a term rather than a state is the new round's closing conditions, which is where the waivers are actually written; the item would be tighter naming that carrier, but the omission is not a defect worth a rewrite.

neighbor_test.left: Threshold that ends independence: drag-along names the coalition, usually the board plus a preferred majority, that can force every holder to sell, and it bites when the investors' clocks diverge from the company's, as the fund past its tenth year that needs distributions and pulls the drag at a price inside the stack where the common takes nothing; not the minority's same-price protection but the trigger and whose clock sets it, and it is worthless without a buyer, who knows this and prices the drag into the offer.
neighbor_test.right: Successor in the chair: a term is held by an entity and exercised by whoever the entity has become when the state arrives, so the veto priced against a friendly partner is pulled by that partner's replacement, by a fund in wind-down that needs distributions, by a secondary buyer who took the position at a discount and breaks even at a different price, or by a continuation vehicle with a fresh clock, as the drag that was a courtesy at signing and a sale order twelve years later; not the term but the replacement of its holder, and the counterparty of the term was never the counterparty of the negotiation.
neighbor_test.separating_case: Chosen because both items illustrate with the same case, a fund past its tenth year pulling the drag. A secondary buyer takes a Series B position at forty cents on the dollar from a fund that is neither old nor distressed, and six months later votes its drag at a price that returns its own basis and nothing to the common: Successor in the chair bites, and Threshold that ends independence does not, since no clock has diverged from the company's. Conversely the original fund, same partner, same pen, at year eleven with limited partners demanding distributions: the drag bites by clock divergence and no successor exists. As written the successor item includes 'a fund in wind-down that needs distributions', which is the second case, so the pair collapses on that phrase alone; with the phrase struck and the cut named (same holder aged versus different holder), the two separate cleanly and the second case is the drag item's own.

boundary_case: Broad-based weighted-average anti-dilution, the term that appears in nearly every priced round and is the respectable sibling of the full ratchet. It is tempting: it bites in the down round, it has a holder, it moves ownership without a vote, and the ratchet is admitted. It is out. It self-executes at its written formula in every state and is almost never the object of a waiver negotiation on its own, because it does not wipe the common; it carries exactly its price, which is dilution-carriers' territory, and the map's test for admission turns out to be whether the term's exercise is renegotiated in the state it was written for. That test admits the ratchet, the redemption demand, the veto, the drag, and the MFN, and it is the same test on which Dividend in the drawer fails.

seriation.note: The axis has real endpoints (a term armed by nothing but the calendar; a term exercised by someone who never priced it), and the declared teaching adjacency Claim on the middle → Flat where the founder is steep does teach: where the claim exists versus where its slope is zero, with the band between them the modal disagreement over a sale. One stop is mis-assigned and it matters because an edge is built on it: Threshold that quietly disenfranchises is filed under 'nothing but the calendar', but a threshold is crossed only when a later issuance dilutes the holder below the line, which is an outside arrival, the third stop. The itinerary reads consistently if the first stop is defined as 'armed by the calendar' (a dividend accrues, a redemption date arrives) and the threshold moves to the arrival stop beside the next round that redefines it. With that move the edge New money rewrites the old paper → Threshold that quietly disenfranchises stops being 'the last stop reaching back to the first' and becomes a dependency within the arrival stop, which is what it actually is; the form inference should drop the reach-back claim. With Dividend in the drawer cut, Redemption clock opens the route and the note's opening sentence needs the substitution.

edges.from_handle: First to know it is dying
edges.why: The antecedent and the first consequent are real: the information lag is what makes the refusal informative. The closing arc of the claimed loop is not. NVCA-form rights of first refusal burden key holders' transfers, not the investors' preferred, so the insiders' own positions never pass through the gate they hold; and funds carry positions at the last round's price, so a founder's discounted secondary does not 'return as a lower mark' on the insiders. The relation is a dependency, not a loop, and the form inference's loop claim should be struck.
edges.repair_label: If the refusal right sits with the holders who also receive the reports, then the outsider bids only for the case in which those holders chose not to match, so the information lag is what gives the refusal its price; strip the lag (reports shared with every holder and with the buyer) and the refusal becomes a courtesy and the outsider's discount vanishes. The refusal depends on the lag; nothing returns to the insiders' book.

edges.why: The passage from the term to its holder is real and the antecedent can fail (the position does not change hands). The final clause, 'no wording of the veto prevents it', is contradicted by the map's own wild priority, which proposes a consent right over transfers of the preferred or a sunset at fund year ten as the clause that would keep the term with the party who priced it. The label should say where the prevention lives rather than deny it exists.
edges.repair_label: If the class veto was priced against the partner in the room and the position changes hands before the rescue round, then the veto is pulled by a holder with a different basis and clock who never priced it; the passage is from the term to its holder, and no wording inside the veto prevents it, only a clause outside it, on transfer of the position or on the veto's own expiry, which is why the term sheet and the fund's partnership agreement are priced against each other by nobody.

edges.from_handle: New money rewrites the old paper
edges.why: The conditional is real and its antecedent can fail (the new lead's paper leaves the major-investor definition alone). The closing clause, 'the last stop of the itinerary reaches back to the first', is an artifact of filing the threshold under the calendar stop; once the threshold sits at the arrival stop where its mechanism actually lives, this is a dependency between two arrival terms, still worth drawing because the strip happens one round before the state in which the rights would have been used.
edges.repair_label: If the new lead's paper raises the major-investor line, then the earlier holders lose their information and pro rata rights one round before the state in which they would have used them; the rewriting is silent because the powers vanish by definition rather than by vote, and the same arrival that supplies the state decides who is still entitled to see it.

modality_problems: First to know it is dying asserts that the company 'never sends the reports and is never made to, which is most companies until the state arrives'; 'most companies' is an unsupported frequency claim promoted to fact and should read as the author's observation.

Chair that owes the room says the seat 'becomes a liability in the very state it was taken for, as litigated in the Trados sale'; in Trados the preferred's directors were found to have run an unfair process but prevailed because the common's shares had no value, so the exposure is an entire-fairness trial, not a loss; the item's 'litigated' is accurate and 'liability' should be read as exposure, which a one-word touch ('an exposure') would fix.

Ratchet that must be waived states as necessity that 'the round the ratchet was written for is the round in which it must be waived'; this is the usual case and not the only one, since a ratchet holder that itself leads the down round keeps the ratchet and rebuilds management incentive from a new pool, so 'must' should be 'is usually'.

Dividend in the drawer's 'roughly one and two-thirds after seven years' assumes compounding that NVCA-form cumulative dividends do not have by default (simple accrual gives about 1.56x); moot if the item is cut.

Redemption clock's reading of ThoughtWorks (the demand yielded a determination rather than a payment; the board decides what funds are legally available, subject to good faith) is accurate to SV Investment Partners v. ThoughtWorks and its modality is kept visible; no repair.
The recapitalization in New money rewrites the old paper and the twelve-year drag in Successor in the chair are readings of common practice, and the mode field says so; no repair.
duplication: Against admitted grown lists: Reserves test in loyalty's clothing overlaps clean-exits' Fade by formula, which uses venture pay-to-play as its illustration, and the item did not say what it adds (repaired above). Threshold that ends independence borders clean-exits' Drag and tag and discriminates itself explicitly; Pass that stamps the sale borders what-a-price-does' Price for the stranger's eyes and discriminates itself explicitly; No-shop and tag-along were correctly refused to lead-time-floors and clean-exits in the residue. Against siblings in this same fleet, which the atlas will hold together if all are admitted: Dividend in the drawer is a near-verbatim duplicate of dilution-carriers' Dividend nobody pays (cut above); Claim on the middle and dilution-carriers' Stack that eats the common plus Carve-out at the door describe the same state from the drain side and the power side; Ratchet that must be waived and Ratchet after the fact, Veto priced by the clock and Veto without votes (and power-trades' Veto sold as an improbability), Fired into the cliff and Reset with the trigger in the other hand are the same terms read for a different question, and each of this map's versions adds something (the waiver value, the clock pricing, the voting-agreement precondition), so they stand, but a one-clause cross-reference in each would save the atlas reader from reading the term twice. Power-law-behaviors' Pockets, not opinion already cites this map's pro rata and pay-to-play items by name; the dependency runs the right way.
best_unresolved_seed: The price of a waiver. The changed question landed on terms whose whole value is what their holder is paid to forgive them (the ratchet, the redemption demand, the class veto, the MFN, the accrued dividend on conversion, the drag's consent), and the author rightly refused 'waiver as the payoff' as a generalization; but the map never says what a waiver is paid in and what sets the rate: a board seat, a fee, a gentler formula, a bigger allocation, a liability release, a sunset, and whether the rate is set by the state's supplier or by the slowest holder. A short map of waiver currencies, seriated by whether the waiver is bought once or must be bought again at every later arrival, is the thing this map most obviously points at and does not contain, and it is where Successor in the chair would finally be priced.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after cutting one item that was a drain rather than a power and duplicated a sibling, repairing the reversed causal order in the refusal-right item and the successor item's overlap with the drag, adding a missing discriminator against clean-exits, relabeling three edges (the claimed loop is a dependency, the veto passage is preventable by a clause outside the veto, and the reach-back to the first stop was an artifact of misfiling the threshold on the seriation).
